passages.original: Cum autem nativitas Christianorum in baptismo sit, baptismi autem generatio et san- ctificatio apud solam Sponsam Christi sit, quae pa- rere spiritaliter et generare filios Deo possit, ubi et ex qua et cui natus est qui filius Ecclesiae non est, ut habere quis possit Deum Patrem ante Eccle- siam matrem (94)? Cum vero 1133 nulla omnino haeresis, sed neque aliquod schisma habere saluta- ris baptismi sanctificationem foris possit, cur in tantum Stephani fratris nostri obstinatio (95) dura prorupit ut etiam de Marcionis baptismo, item Va- lentini et Apelletis, et caeterurum blasphemantium in Deum Patrem contendat filios Deo nasci, et illic in nomine Jcsn Christi dicat remissionem peccato- rum dari ubi blasphematur in Patrem et in Domi- num Deum Christum?
passages.english: Now since the birth of Christians is in baptism, and the generation and sanctification of baptism is with the Bride of Christ alone, who is able to bear spiritually and to beget sons to God, where, and of whom, and to whom has he been born who is not a son of the Church, so that anyone could have God as Father before [he has] the Church as mother? And since no heresy at all, nor indeed any schism, can have the sanctification of saving baptism outside, why has the hard obstinacy of our brother Stephen broken out to such an extent that he contends that sons are born to God even from the baptism of Marcion, and likewise of Valentinus and Apelles, and of the others who blaspheme against God the Father, and says that remission of sins is given there in the name of Jesus Christ, where blasphemy is uttered against the Father and against the Lord God Christ?
passages.notes: Numbers in parentheses (94), (95) and the figure 1133 are editorial note markers or page numbers and have been omitted. Scanning errors corrected: 'Jcsn' for 'Jesu', 'caeterurum' for 'caeterorum'.
